risk_if_not_implemented: Without Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Evidence Integrity & Provenance, automated control assurance results may be manipulated, misattributed or lose integrity, causing misplaced confidence in control effectiveness. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), Loss of Investigative / Evidentiary Capability (R-IR-1), Loss of Data Integrity (R-IP-3), Loss of Authenticity / Provenance (R-IP-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14).

compensating_control_1.name: Protection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to protect event logs, security-relevant telemetry and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion.
compensating_control_1.justification: Protection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry (MON-12) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Evidence Integrity & Provenance (CPL-30) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Evidence Request List (ERL)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to define an Evidence Request List (ERL) prior to the start of a cybersecurity and/or data protection assessment.
compensating_control_2.justification: Evidence Request List (ERL) (CPL-16) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Evidence Integrity & Provenance (CPL-30) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
